_comment: The example pre-read config. Copy to <helm home>/_global/preread.json and
edit: this file is documentation and is never read at runtime. Every
endpoint, model name, host and key lives here, so helm/preread.py carries
none of them and a fleet re-points its readers without a code change.
readers: the council. One entry per ENDPOINT; `seeds` is how many drafts
that endpoint writes per file (one call per seed, seeded so a draft is
reproducible). `think` false sends chat_template_kwargs
{"enable_thinking": false}: a thinking model that exhausts max_tokens
inside its reasoning returns EMPTY content, which reads as a clean file.
`max_tokens` and `repeat_penalty` are the repetition guard - an unguarded
weak reader degenerates into a loop past a few thousand tokens.
judge: a DIFFERENT model from the readers. It refuses the false classes
the readers are prone to and writes down what it dropped. It is asked per
FILE and then once more to merge the judged lists, because one judge call
over a whole change's drafts answers NONE FOUND and discards true
findings it never had room to read.
key_from: a file whose `api-key:` line carries the judge's bearer token.
helm reads it narrowly and hands it to exactly one request; nothing
prints, logs or stores it.
checklist: the defect classes sent with every file (docs/preread-checklist.md).
cap_bytes: per-file diff bound; a bigger file is sent truncated and said so.
trunk: the ref the row's tip is diffed against, via its merge base.
